shape.description: Orange open-frame tower, one cell square, two tiers. Top tier: a dished cup with a U notch on each of its four sides and a hole in the middle, four corner posts rising into crown points that hold a block above. Bottom tier: a cup with a U notch on two opposite sides and a T-shaped flap on a pivot in the middle. Arched block feet nest on a block below. Open windows between the tiers.
shape.sizeBasis: Height from the ports: the top tier's rim stands 0.17 slot over the stack-top port at 2 slots (as a block's rails do), the crown points about 10 mm higher; the photo's height-to-width ratio (about 1.6) stays an open question. Grid scale (2026-11-07): one cell 45 mm, one slot 45.3 mm (B-01, src/catalog/parts.js). The earlier figure used a 52 mm cell and a 36 mm slot, which disagreed with this record's own ports and heightSlots.

physics.behaviour: Two-tier switch. A marble comes in over any of the four notches of the top tier, drops through to the bottom tier and lands on a pivoting T-shaped flap. The flap tips and sends it out one side, and stays tipped, so the next marble goes out the other side: left, right, left, right. The flap can be pushed by hand to choose the first side. Passive; gravity only.

Real piece: two tiers, four U notches on the top tier, a T-shaped flap on a pivot in the bottom tier, crown points, arched feet
Marbles come in from any of four directions on the top tier and fall to the bottom; one M-04 kind sends them randomly one way or the other, the other has a toggle that alternates sides

assumptions: Which set has the toggle: the photographed piece has the pivoting flap and matches the T-Rex parts drawing (crown points, trex_plans_01), and it was photographed with the T-Rex pieces. So the T-Rex mould is the toggle and the Launchpad mould the random splitter. Not confirmed by Joey.
Bottom exits on two opposite sides (E and W in the piece frame); the photo shows one bottom notch facing the camera, the flap pivots across it.

Height kept at 2 slots for stacking: the T-Rex plans need 2 (stacks I7, D3 and A2 all reach h8 at the M-61 outlet). The photo ratio says the rim is about 1.6 slots high, so the real pitch may be 1.5; a side-by-side photo with two stacked blocks would settle it.
Top tier inlets meet a track at level 2 (z 1.68) and bottom exits at level 1 (z 0.68) above what the tower stands on, like a block's cup seat.
Split as a T-Rex file because the Launchpad set also lists M-04.
faces uses E=+x, W=-x, S=+y, N=-y, in the piece's own frame.

marblePaths list the four ways into the E exit (straight through, from either side, and back out the side it came in). The W exit takes the same four, mirrored: the tower is the same turned half round, so the engine turns it instead of listing them twice.
